open_assumptions: The contract's `blocked` status with a null verdict does not distinguish an expired review deadline from a rejected completion file, so the viewer says 'delivered no verdict: the review deadline expired or its completion file was rejected' for both; a dedicated field would be needed to say which.

The fixtures now model run-state.json's review.reviewers[].status as the contract vocabulary, on the reading that workflow/export_state.py maps the controller's own status words (`succeeded` to `accepted`) before writing; the controller's raw words never reach the server.

The run-inputs projection version mismatch (mock stamped 1.4.0, contract pins runInputs at 1.3.0) was a latent fixture defect hidden behind the reviewer-status error in run 001; it is fixed in fixtures.ts, not in the contract.
result.summary: Aligned the viewer with the landed 1.4.0 reviewers contract. Changed files: src/projects/reviewers.ts (STATUS_WORDING is now keyed on the contract's Reviewer['status'] = accepted|blocked|superseded|pending; removed the invented timed_out/rejected/succeeded/needs_reconciliation/launching/running values; blockingReason derives the deadline-or-rejected-file wording from status 'blocked' with verdict null, and outcomeWording derives 'no verdict' wording from verdict/launched_at for superseded and pending entries), src/projects/ReviewDetail.tsx (one doc comment; markup, strip, Reviewer column, filter and blocked-by line were already driven by the helpers and needed no change), tests/project-workflows/fixtures.ts (RawReviewerStatus is now the contract vocabulary as workflow/export_state.py writes it; the two-reviewer approved run uses status 'accepted' and the legacy single-reviewer projection falls back to 'accepted'/'blocked'; split CONTRACT_VERSION into REVIEW_CONTRACT_VERSION '1.4.0' and INPUTS_CONTRACT_VERSION '1.3.0' because the run-inputs mock was stamped 1.4.0 while the contract pins runInputs at 1.3.0, a second config-load failure that run 001's log did not reach because projectReview threw first). tests/project-workflows/seed.ts and reviewers.spec.ts needed no edits: the seed writes the review section from rawReviewSection, so the fixture fix is what the real server reads, and every spec assertion ('completion file accepted', 'blocked the candidate', 'stopped after the combined decision, no verdict', the blocked-by sentence) holds under the real vocabulary. All three fixture runs (both approved; coverage blocked with general superseded; legacy 1.3.0 export projected as one entry named review) stay meaningful. No files under contracts/, server/, workflow/ or features/ were touched. Checks executed in this worktree after npm ci (node_modules were absent): npm run build (exit 0, tsc -b and vite build clean); npm run test:unit (exit 0, 130 tests, 130 pass, 0 fail); WORKFLOW_VERIFICATION_PHASE=worker npx --no-install playwright test --config=tests/project-workflows/playwright.config.ts (exit 0, 20 passed, all 20 scenarios including [scenario:viewer-two-reviewers] with the mocked project routes); WORKFLOW_VERIFICATION_PHASE=candidate same command (exit 0, 20 passed, all 20 scenarios including [scenario:viewer-two-reviewers] against the real server over seeded run folders; the viewer-two-reviewers-blocked screenshot was inspected and shows coverage blocked, general superseded, the blocked-by line and the reviewer filter). Logs live under the job tmp directory; run 001 evidence was read and not modified.
